title: Skynode Partners
subtitle: Turning 99 urban rooftops into a searchable infrastructure platform
intro: We designed and built a 17-route website for Skynode Partners. It brings 99 rooftop infrastructure sites into a searchable catalog, with separate journeys for network operators and building owners.
metadata: Telecom and digital infrastructure (rooftop sites, edge colocation, broadcast, private networks)
Network operators (broadcast, private comms, edge/AI compute, emerging tech) and property owners
Positioning support, information architecture, UX/UI design, front-end development, interactive data views, lead-capture flow
17 routes: home, 4 solution verticals, solutions hub, node catalog, Metro Fabric, 4 market pages, property owners, how it works, about, careers, contact
client: Skynode Partners turns urban rooftops and service space into managed infrastructure sites. Network operators can evaluate locations for their equipment; building owners can explore a partnership that generates recurring revenue from unused space.
verticalIntro: The operator side spans four verticals, each with its own technical buyer:

verticals.title: Broadcasting
verticals.description: FM, TV, LPFM, translators, backup and auxiliary (STL) sites

verticals.title: Private communications
verticals.description: P25 and simulcast radio, private 5G, point-to-point microwave

verticals.title: Edge colocation
verticals.description: AI/GPU inference, CDN and caching, network interconnection, up to 120 kW per rack

verticals.title: Experimental systems
verticals.description: drones, spatial AI sensing, field AR, smart city, metering

fabric: On top of the sites sits Metro Fabric, a private wireless and fiber interconnect that links nodes into one network, with sub-5 ms intra-fabric latency (representative) and a 99.9% target uptime SLA.
challengeIntro: The website needed to explain a technical infrastructure business to engineers, operations teams and property owners. Each audience needed useful detail and a clear path to the right inquiry.

challenges.title: Two audiences with different questions
challenges.description: Operators need elevation, line of sight and network connections. Property owners need to understand access, approvals and the partnership process.

challenges.title: Four technical service areas
challenges.description: Broadcasting, private communications, edge colocation and experimental systems each need relevant specifications and examples.

challenges.title: Real sites visitors can inspect
challenges.description: The catalog needed to show documented locations, services and status so visitors could evaluate a specific rooftop.

challenges.title: Several people involved in a decision
challenges.description: Engineering, operations, finance and leadership all need enough detail to assess the same site.

challenges.title: A network that keeps growing
challenges.description: Sites under evaluation need clear status labels. Unconfirmed specifications must stay visible as per-site details or to-be-confirmed values.

goals: Explain Skynode as a connected infrastructure network.
Help operators find and evaluate a specific site.
Give each service area a relevant landing page.
Explain the owner partnership and make submitting a property straightforward.
Route inquiries by audience, use case and market.
Make it easy to add sites, markets and services.
strategyIntro: The strategy was simple: show real sites and the details buyers need. Every operator page leads toward a rooftop that visitors can inspect and ask about.

strategy.title: Separate journeys from the first click
strategy.description: Solutions and the node catalog serve operators. The property-owner section serves building owners. Both paths reach a shared form that starts by asking which audience the visitor belongs to.

strategy.title: Explain deployment, expansion and operation
strategy.description: The home page shows how an operator can start at one node, expand to more sites and connect through Metro Fabric.

strategy.title: Put technical and commercial detail together
strategy.description: Solution pages pair site criteria such as power, elevation and structural loading with information about access, permitting and pricing.

strategy.title: Label what is still being confirmed
strategy.description: Per-site and to-be-confirmed labels keep uncertain specifications visible. The inquiry process sets an expectation of a human response within one business day.

architecture: Operators browse solutions, markets or Metro Fabric before opening the site catalog. Property owners check fit and share building details. Both journeys reach one form that routes the inquiry by audience and need.

features.title: A searchable catalog of 99 nodes
features.description: Each site card shows its ID, market, neighborhood, elevation, status and supported services. Visitors can filter the catalog and inquire about a specific node.
bullets: Market tabs: All, New York, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois
Service filters: Broadcasting, Private Comms, Edge Colocation, AI / Inference, Point-to-Point
Live result count ("Showing 99 of 99 nodes"), sorted by elevation so the strongest sites surface first
A "Recent node activity" panel with network totals (90 active, 9 evaluating, 4 markets)
A fallback path for gaps: "Don’t see the right node? Tell us what you need"

features.title: Interactive network map
features.description: A Leaflet map shows node locations, market filters and power tiers. The same map is reused across solution and market pages so visitors can compare the network in context.

features.title: Relevant sites on every solution page
features.description: Each solution page shows sites that support that service. Broadcast visitors can inspect elevation; edge-computing visitors can compare power density and service tiers.

features.title: Metro Fabric visualizations
features.description: Canvas and SVG network diagrams explain how cloud connections, Metro Fabric and private links work together. A comparison covers capacity, pricing, redundancy and routing.

features.title: A skyline hero that introduces the network
features.description: A city-skyline animation sits beside a Metro Fabric network panel. Market and service labels introduce the network before visitors explore individual sites.

features.title: Segmented, multi-step inquiry form
features.description: The form begins with two choices: infrastructure or property ownership. Follow-up steps collect the segment, use case and market so the team has useful context before replying.

features.title: Market pages
features.description: New York, Connecticut, Florida and Illinois each have a page with local services, representative sites and market details.

features.title: Property-owner qualification
features.description: A property-fit summary and checklist help owners review elevation, utilities, space and market before sending their building details.

features.title: Light and dark themes
features.description: A persistent header toggle lets visitors choose a light or dark reading mode for the website.

designIntro: An open layout, navy headings and blue accents give technical information a clear hierarchy. Site data, filters and status labels stay easy to scan.

design.title: Palette
design.description: Pale sky-blue backgrounds, deep navy headlines and a single teal-blue accent for key words and primary buttons. Soft greens signal "Active" and "Network Operational"; amber marks "Evaluating".

design.title: Typography
design.description: Satoshi throughout, with heavy, tightly set headlines that split into a navy line and a teal line ("Infrastructure for the / Metropolitan Edge.").

design.title: Signature motifs
design.description: Translucent 3D skyline columns, hexagonal grids and node-and-link network lines — the rooftop-to-network idea drawn directly into the backgrounds.

design.title: Service tag system
design.description: Each service has a consistent color-coded pill (Broadcasting, Private Comms, Edge Colocation, AI / Inference, P2P, IoT / Sensors) used on cards, maps and filters, so a visitor learns the code once and reads every node at a glance.

design.title: Glass panels
design.description: Status and data panels use frosted, rounded cards with live indicators, echoing a network operations dashboard.

design.title: Reusable section rhythm
design.description: Eyebrow label → two-tone headline → short lead → proof grid → node strip → CTA band. The same rhythm across 17 routes makes the site feel like one product.

technology: Component reuse across 17 routes; instant client-side navigation between catalog, verticals and markets
Client-side routes per vertical and per market (/markets/new-york)
Clean, shareable URLs for each audience and campaign
Leaflet with a custom hex node layer and power-tier legend
Lightweight, open-source, no heavy GIS dependency
HTML canvas (3D skyline, network animations) plus 100+ inline SVGs
Rich visuals with no video weight; crisp at any resolution
Structured node records (ID, market, neighborhood, elevation, status, services, power tier)
One dataset drives the catalog, map, vertical strips, market pages and counts
Light / dark toggle on design tokens
Multi-step form with segment, use case and market steps
Per-route titles, meta description, Open Graph tags
Correct titles and link previews for every page

engineering.title: Data-driven by design
engineering.description: One set of node records feeds the catalog, map, solution pages, market pages and headline counts. A new site can be added once and appear wherever it meets the filters.

engineering.title: Reusable building blocks
engineering.description: Shared maps, filters, site cards, service labels and inquiry sections keep behavior consistent across the four solution pages and four market pages.

copyIntro: The content uses direct language, practical site details and clear explanations of the next step.

messaging.title: A sharp core line
messaging.description: "Infrastructure for the Metropolitan Edge", backed by the idea that the best edge sites are inside the city, not near it.

messaging.title: Physics as the argument
messaging.description: The edge page sells latency with plain math — compute three states away costs about 40 ms round trip; a metro node gets under 5 ms.

messaging.title: Pain first, then relief
messaging.description: The broadcast page opens on the old way (blank maps, cold landlord calls, dead-end RF surveys) before showing that viable candidates already exist.

messaging.title: Risk language for owners
messaging.description: The property-owner page leads with what landlords fear — paperwork, liability, approvals — and answers with managed permitting across local, state and federal levels.

messaging.title: Plain FAQs
messaging.description: Eight questions on How It Works cover timelines, minimum deployment (none), pricing model and what happens when a node goes offline.

messaging.title: Consistent promises
messaging.description: "A real person reviews every inquiry within one business day" repeats on every vertical and conversion page.

resultIntro: The delivered website gives Skynode a working catalog and clear inquiry paths for both audiences:
results: 99 nodes published and filterable across 4 markets, each with its own inquiry path
4 vertical landing pages plus a solutions hub, each speaking to its own technical buyer
2 complete funnels (operators and property owners) on one domain
4 market pages ready for regional campaigns and outreach
A pre-qualified lead flow that captures segment, use case and market before the first call
A reusable component and data model that lets the team add nodes and markets without new design work
measurementNote: These are delivery outcomes. Inquiry growth, qualification rates, property submissions, performance scores and client feedback were not supplied, so no measured uplift is claimed.
roadmapIntro: The shared components and site data provide a foundation for these next steps:
roadmap: Node detail pages with photos, line-of-sight views and downloadable spec sheets
A CMS or admin panel so the Skynode team can add and update nodes themselves
CRM integration so routed inquiries land directly in the sales pipeline
Gated operator portal for availability, documents and deployment status
New markets (Miami and Chicago Metro Fabric are already flagged as ready for rapid deployment)
